<rationale>
Order the four random points cyclically on the radius-2 circle. The four adjacent angular gaps, normalized to sum \(1\), are uniformly distributed on the simplex (Dirichlet \((1,1,1,1)\)). A side/chord with circular gap \(x\) has distance \(2|\cos(\pi x)|\) from the center, so it intersects the radius-1 circle iff \(2|\cos(\pi x)|<1\), i.e. \(x\in(1/3,2/3)\).

Thus the desired event is \(\exists i: 1/3<X_i<2/3\). Its complement is that every gap is either \(\le 1/3\) or at least one gap is \(\ge 2/3\). These cases are disjoint. For the uniform simplex:
\[
P(\max X_i\le 1/3)=(1/3)^3=1/27
\]
by shifting coordinates, and
\[
P(\max X_i\ge 2/3)=4P(X_1\ge 2/3)=4(1/3)^3=4/27.
\]
Hence the no-intersection probability is \(1/27+4/27=5/27\), so the intersection probability is \(1-5/27=22/27\).
</rationale>
<final>
\boxed{\frac{22}{27}}
</final>
